text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Tough negotiations over lira's return to EMS. The talks turned out to be more difficult than expected. While Italy wanted rate of 1,010 lira per mark, French-led majority demanded a much higher value for the lira.
- Chancellor Kohl wants stability criteria for EMU to be valid also in the years beyond start of EMU. Kohl pledges to push for timely start of currency union as well as holding to stability criteria.
- Labour Minister Bluem suggests that pension level could decline after reform programme completed.
- No decision from Stuttgart meeting on international aid relief programme for Zaire.
HANDELSBLATT

- New dispute over proposed tax on investment earnings. CSU party congress rejects general trax on speculation profits on property and securities. That contrasts with sister party CDU, which at a recent party congress called for such a tax.
- New optimism on the German bourse. Many analysts expect DAX to continue gaining this week.
- SPD leader Lafontaine says government neglecting training and education for younger Germans.
- Western German industry reports lively demand, according to IFO report. Signs of a strengthening economic upturn increase in October.

- Iran owes Germany 13 billion marks and this is one reason German government eager to maintain diplomatic relations with Tehran. Foreign Minister Kinkel says that Bonn being led by, among other things, economic motives in this issue.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- SPD parliamentary leader Scharping wants new SPD focus in foreign policy, one that is for the most part in line with government's.
- Kohl rejects idea of grand coalition with SPD, tells CSU party congress in Munich that SPD not fit for governing.
- Oil industry says environmental protectio has to be linked to cost/use analysis.
DIE WELT
- CDU ready to make compromise on solidarity surcharge tax. Coalition considering two-point cut in tax rate in 1998.
- Hard negotiations for lira's return into EMS.
